title: Plurimath conformance case group, with per-target outcomes
description: One file of conformance cases for a single input format, grouped by feature, where every target carries an OUTCOME rather than a string. Payloads declare `plurimath-corpus/<input_format>/2`. This exists because `cases/1` cannot say `this target raises`: it holds one `targets` list for the group and demands a rendered string from every case for every target, so an input the gem ACCEPTS but renders to only SOME targets has no representation there and was simply left out — and an input left out is an input a port may refuse while still passing. Measured example: `sqrt(` parses, renders to asciimath, latex and mathml, and raises `Plurimath::Math::ParseError` from `to_unicodemath` (cause `NoMethodError`, wrapped by `Math::Formula#wrap_render_error`). `cases/1` is NOT superseded and NOT converted: a group whose every case renders to every target stays there, and a consumer that understands only `cases/1` keeps working, because a payload names its own schema and scripts/validate.rb dispatches on that name.

schema.description: Schema this payload follows. The middle segment is the input format, so an AsciiMath group declares `plurimath-corpus/asciimath/2`. The trailing `2` is the shape of `expected`, nothing else: every other field means exactly what it means in `cases/1`.

group.description: Feature group; matches the file name without its extension. A schema cannot see the file name, so scripts/validate.rb enforces the match.

input_format.description: Agrees with the `schema` declaration's middle segment, with the directory the file sits in, and with every case's `input_format`; scripts/validate.rb reconciles all four.

targets.description: Output formats every case in this group carries an OUTCOME for. Still one list for the whole group, and still exhaustive per case — what changed is that an outcome may be a refusal, so a target no longer has to render for the case to be recorded. JSON Schema cannot compare two fields, so scripts/validate.rb — not this schema — reconciles this list with each case's `expected` keys.

class_name.description: A Plurimath model class, with the `Plurimath::` prefix stripped.

error_category.description: What rendering this target did, at the coarseness the gem's public boundary exposes. `parse_error` is the only value, and — as in `rejections/1` — deliberately so: `Math::Formula#to_unicodemath` and its siblings funnel every render failure through `wrap_render_error`, which re-raises `Math::ParseError`. Measured on `sqrt(`: the raised class is `Plurimath::Math::ParseError` and the underlying `NoMethodError` survives only as `#cause`. The category is therefore PORTABLE by construction — it names what the boundary says, not the Ruby class that failed behind it. A port raising its own equivalent at its own boundary is conformant; a port that renders something here is not. Which target and which operation is already said by the key this outcome sits under, so the category does not repeat it.

outcome.description: What one target did with this case: EXACTLY ONE of a rendering or a refusal. `oneOf` with `additionalProperties: false` in both branches is what makes that exhaustive and exclusive — an outcome carrying both keys matches neither branch, and so does an empty one, so the two states cannot blur into a third. `type: object` sits INSIDE each branch rather than beside the `oneOf`: a bare string, which is what `cases/1` writes at this position, is not an object, so it fails both branches and is reported as matching neither. Hoisted out, the string would instead satisfy both branches vacuously — object keywords say nothing about a string — and the report would read `matches 2 of the oneOf alternatives`, which describes the validator rather than the defect.

output.description: Exactly the bytes the gem produced for this target. Compared byte for byte, as in `cases/1`.

error.description: The target refused to render. There is no `index` here, unlike `rejections/1`: an offset would point into `preprocessed`, and by the time a target renders, `preprocessed` has already parsed successfully — the failure is downstream of the text and no position in it describes the failure. `additionalProperties: false` keeps one from being invented.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique within the group; scripts/validate.rb enforces the uniqueness, which one schema item cannot see of its siblings.

input_format.description: Equals the group's `input_format`; scripts/validate.rb enforces the agreement.

preprocessed.description: The input after the format's preprocessing pass, which may shift offsets.

expected.description: Outcome per target format. The keys are exactly the group's `targets` — a constraint between two fields, so scripts/validate.rb checks it rather than this schema, which can only require the keys to be target formats at all. `parse_tree` and `model` are still required beside this, and are still meaningful when a target refused: the input parsed, so there is a tree and a model to reproduce; only the rendering of that model failed.

parse_tree.description: The parser's tree, serialized as plain data. Numbers and booleans are excluded deliberately: no parse tree has ever produced one, so a new scalar kind should be a validation failure rather than a silent shape change.

node.description: A Plurimath::Math::Core node: its class, and its instance variables serialized by name.

object_field_value.description: An object-valued field is either a nested node or a plain map such as `options` or `attributes`. A `class` key means it claims to be a node, so it must be a well-formed one.
